subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should deferred background context-engine maintenance remain unbounded by default with an operator opt-in timeout, or should OpenClaw own a finite default timeout policy?
rationale: The patch is structured around a new disabled-by-default configuration key, but repository policy treats new config, plugin runtime limits, and fallback behavior as product contracts that source review alone cannot permanently choose.

options.title: Keep opt-in timeout
options.body: Accept the disabled-by-default key so affected operators can bound wedged maintenance without changing existing plugin behavior on upgrade.

options.title: Choose a finite default
options.body: Define a host-owned default budget and prove upgrade safety for legitimate long-running context engines before merge.

options.title: Reuse existing policy
options.body: Reject the new key and redesign the fix around an existing compaction or session-recovery timeout after proving that contract fits deferred maintenance.

recommendation.title: Keep opt-in timeout
recommendation.body: Accept the disabled-by-default key so affected operators can bound wedged maintenance without changing existing plugin behavior on upgrade.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the background maintenance lifecycle and are the strongest available owner for its timeout and plugin-compatibility contract.
